title: Double take
rule: Vaudeville timing: a double take at the clock, a near miss with the cupboard door, no fall; the gag is the forgetting.
declares: keeps E0-E5, the four lines and the outcome
build: films/swarm/99-ways/build/p14_double_take.py (the plate: build/p07_two_panels.py; brush: build/brushkit.py; figures: build/b1m2.py)
made: the ONE HANDMADE brush plate of the office made for page 07 (dab-chain brush after the moins-dun-quart-de-seconde-pour-vivre plate method), printed again unchanged in all nine panels and framed by camera crops; plate ink sha256 a2b261037f7e77a12e22de2421bc85ab942cbdbf5f8272d1c58db6a6308024e4
brushed figures from the b1m2 model; a head-turn rig made here (the head of a right-facing figure pinned at the neck of a left-facing body) for the glance, the look away and the snap back
brushed whip lines round the snapping head (P5); brushed swoosh arcs tracing the cupboard leaf's swing (P7)
a pasted paper overlay opening the cupboard on its left jamb, the leaf at 250 px for the near miss and 112 px at rest; the ANRC 1922 key printed in ink on its hook with a SERVICE tag
timing slips in the pen hand ('a glance...', 'away...', 'and back!', 'whoosh... missed!', 'beat.'), brushed balloons with the four canon lines; folio by pen99.folio

P2 and P6: the stranger seen THROUGH the ticket window (behind_glass in p14_double_take.py): a pale cool platform wash with the platform edge, the far eave and a canopy post brushed in the opening; her figure laid into the opening and cut off at the sill; then the plate's own window frame and both mullions re-laid in ink over her, and brushed white glass glints across the panes and her coat

events.E0: P1 seated at the desk behind the memo slip ('4:15 - open SERVICE door. Key in cupboard.'); P2 he is up and walking toward the cupboard
events.E1: P2 the stranger outside on the platform, seen through the TICKET OFFICE window (the mullions cross her), question balloon; he looks back over his shoulder
events.E2: P3 a glance up at the clock; P4 head back to the window; P5 head snaps back to the clock (the double take, whip lines) and the answer; the clock reads 4:10 in every crop
events.E3: P6 she turns away behind the glass, thanks balloon tailed to the window's edge
events.E4: P7 he pulls the cupboard open; the leaf swings out and stops a whisker from his nose, he leans back, no fall (the near miss); key on its hook; P8 held beat on the key
events.E5: P9 in the open doorway, pencil to his chin, the forgetting line; key unmoved; SERVICE door closed

lines.question: Pardon me — have you the right time?
lines.answer: Ten past four, by the clock.
lines.forgetting: Well, here I am... and what for?

beat: row 2: the head is away from the clock, then snaps back to it with whip lines, then the answer is laid; row 3: the cupboard leaf swings out toward his nose and he leans back
beat_frames: b01: P5 head still away from the clock (no answer), cupboard closed in P7
b02: P5 head snapped back to the clock with whip lines
b04: P7 leaf half out (120 px), he begins to lean
b05: leaf full out, a whisker from his nose, swoosh lines
b06: + forgetting balloon in P9 (the finished page)

self_check.double_take: P3 head to the clock (tilt -20), P4 head back to the window, P5 head to the clock again (tilt -30) with whip lines: two head turns to the clock in consecutive takes
self_check.check: A reader finds the double take (two consecutive head turns to the clock). -> row 2 shows the turn to the clock, the look away and the snap back (maker's judgement from the full-size page; blind reading pending)
self_check.evidence: measured (size, pixel checks named in the repair) and judged from the full-size page by the repair maker; a fresh blind reading of the repair is pending
self_check.plate_prints_note: the plate itself is laid unchanged in all nine panels (hash as before); in P2 and P6 its window region is re-laid a second time over the stranger so the mullions cross her

weaknesses: the check asks for two consecutive head turns to the clock; the page puts a look-away panel between them (glance, away, back), which is the classic double take but a strict reader may count panels differently
the near miss reads as 'leaning back from the swinging door' rather than a sharp gag; the stopped leaf and his face overlap in silhouette scale
the plate is page 07's plate, so the set is identical to page 07 by design (one repeated plate); the page differs by camera crops and timing
P1 crops the clock's pendulum oddly at the top edge

changed: P2, P6: platform wash behind her, figure clipped to the window opening at the sill, the plate's frame and mullions re-laid over her, white glass glints over her silhouette
P6 thanks-balloon tail now ends at the window's right edge instead of crossing her face
repairs.pass_test: a blind reader calls her a traveller or passenger at the window, not a clerk, and the mullion lines visibly cross her silhouette
